records.literal_gloss: And he gave understanding and spoke with me and said: Daniel, now I have come out to make you wise [in] understanding.

en.L: And he instructed me and spoke with me and said, "Daniel, I have now come out to give you insight and understanding.
en.B: He explained things to me and said, "Daniel, I have now come to give you insight and understanding.
en.R: He explained things to me. He said, "Daniel, I have come to help you understand.

fr.L: Et il [m’]instruisit, et il parla avec moi et dit : « Daniel, je suis maintenant sorti pour te donner la sagesse et l’intelligence.
fr.B: Il m’expliqua les choses et me dit : « Daniel, je suis venu maintenant pour te donner discernement et intelligence.
fr.R: Il m’a expliqué les choses. Il m’a dit : « Daniel, je suis venu t’aider à comprendre.

es.L: Y me instruyó, y habló conmigo y dijo: «Daniel, ahora he salido para darte sabiduría y entendimiento.
es.B: Me explicó las cosas y me dijo: «Daniel, ahora he venido para darte sabiduría y entendimiento.
es.R: Me explicó las cosas. Me dijo: «Daniel, he venido para ayudarte a entender.

decisions.choice: he gave understanding: he instructed me
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone understand. Some ancient translations read "he came" here, a different but similar word.

decisions.choice: Gabriel's words in quotation marks
decisions.reason: Gabriel's speech, set in double quotation marks, runs to the end of verse 27.

decisions.choice: Gabriel's words (verses 22-27) are one quotation, opened here and closed at verse 27
alternatives: closing the quotation at each verse
decisions.reason: As the term sheet asks for Daniel's angelic speeches, as in 8:19-26.

decisions.choice: the « opens here and closes at the end of verse 27
decisions.reason: Gabriel's words run over several verses and are not closed and reopened at each verse

source.text: בִּתְחִלַּ֨ת תַּחֲנוּנֶ֜יךָ יָצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר וַאֲנִי֙ בָּ֣אתִי לְהַגִּ֔יד כִּ֥י חֲמוּד֖וֹת אָ֑תָּה וּבִין֙ בַּדָּבָ֔ר וְהָבֵ֖ן בַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: At [the] beginning of your supplications a word went out, and I have come to tell, for precious [are] you; and understand the word and have understanding in the vision.

en.L: At the beginning of your pleas a word went out, and I have come to tell [it], for you are greatly loved. So consider the word and understand the vision.
en.B: As soon as you began to plead, an answer was given, and I have come to tell it to you, for you are greatly loved. So pay attention to the message and understand the vision.
en.R: As soon as you began to pray, God gave an answer. I have come to tell it to you, because God loves you very much. So think about this message and understand the vision.

fr.L: Au commencement de tes supplications une parole est sortie, et je suis venu [te l’]annoncer, car tu es [un homme] bien-aimé. Sois donc attentif à la parole et comprends la vision.
fr.B: Dès que tu as commencé à supplier, une réponse a été donnée, et je suis venu te la faire connaître, car tu es tant aimé. Sois donc attentif à ce message et comprends la vision.
fr.R: Dès que tu as commencé à prier, Dieu a donné une réponse. Je suis venu te la dire, parce que Dieu t’aime beaucoup. Réfléchis donc à ce message et comprends la vision.

es.L: Al principio de tus súplicas salió una palabra, y yo he venido para anunciar[la], porque tú eres muy amado. Considera, pues, la palabra y entiende la visión.
es.B: En cuanto comenzaste a suplicar, se dio una respuesta, y he venido a comunicártela, porque eres muy amado. Presta atención, pues, al mensaje y entiende la visión.
es.R: En cuanto empezaste a orar, Dios dio una respuesta. He venido a decírtela, porque Dios te ama mucho. Así que piensa en este mensaje y entiende la visión.

decisions.choice: a word went out: a command or answer was given in heaven
decisions.reason: "Word" may be God's answer to the prayer or his command to Gabriel. It went out at once, at the start of the prayer.

decisions.choice: you are greatly loved: you are precious, highly treasured
decisions.reason: The word means something desired and precious (Genesis 27:15; 2 Chronicles 20:25). The same is said of Daniel in 10:11 and 19. It is God who treasures him.

decisions.choice: the vision: the revelation that follows
decisions.reason: The "vision" is the message about the seventy sevens (verses 24-27), which comes as words, not as a picture.

decisions.choice: God gave an answer; God loves you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who gave the word and who loves Daniel; the Hebrew leaves both implied.

decisions.choice: "tu es [un homme] bien-aimé" (L), "tu es tant aimé" (B), "Dieu t'aime beaucoup" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the angel's "man greatly loved" (10:11, 19), used here for the shorter form; Readable says who loves him, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "eres muy amado" (L, B); "Dios te ama mucho" (R)
decisions.reason: As the angel's "hombre muy amado" of 10:11, 19; R says who loves him, as the English R does

source.text: שָׁבֻעִ֨ים שִׁבְעִ֜ים נֶחְתַּ֥ךְ עַֽל־עַמְּךָ֣׀וְעַל־עִ֣יר קָדְשֶׁ֗ךָ לְכַלֵּ֨א הַפֶּ֜שַׁע וּלְהָתֵ֤ם חַטָּאת֙ וּלְכַפֵּ֣ר עָוֺ֔ן וּלְהָבִ֖יא צֶ֣דֶק עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וְלַחְתֹּם֙ חָז֣וֹן וְנָבִ֔יא וְלִמְשֹׁ֖חַ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: Sevens seventy have been decreed for your people and for your holy city, to finish the transgression and to seal up sin and to atone for iniquity and to bring righteousness of perpetuity and to seal up vision and prophet and to anoint a holy of holies.

en.L: Seventy sevens have been decreed for your people and for your holy city: to finish the transgression, and to seal up sin, and to atone for iniquity, and to bring everlasting righteousness, and to seal vision and prophet, and to anoint a most holy [place].
en.B: Seventy sevens have been decreed for your people and your holy city, to put an end to rebellion, to bring sin to a close, to atone for wrongdoing, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to put a seal on vision and prophecy, and to anoint a most holy place.
en.R: God has set a time of seventy sets of seven for your people and your holy city. In that time God will end their rebellion. He will finish with sin. He will take away guilt. He will bring in righteousness that will last forever. He will make the vision and the prophecy come true. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set apart a most holy place for God.

fr.L: Soixante-dix septaines ont été fixées sur ton peuple et sur ta ville sainte, pour faire cesser la transgression, et pour sceller le péché, et pour expier l’iniquité, et pour amener une justice éternelle, et pour sceller vision et prophète, et pour oindre un saint des saints.
fr.B: Soixante-dix septaines ont été fixées pour ton peuple et pour ta ville sainte, pour mettre fin à la rébellion, pour en finir avec le péché, pour expier la faute, pour faire venir une justice éternelle, pour mettre un sceau sur la vision et la prophétie, et pour oindre un lieu très saint.
fr.R: Dieu a fixé un temps de soixante-dix périodes de sept pour ton peuple et pour ta ville sainte. Pendant ce temps, Dieu mettra fin à leur révolte. Il en finira avec le péché. Il enlèvera la faute. Il fera venir une justice qui durera toujours. Il accomplira la vision et la prophétie. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} consacrera à Dieu un lieu très saint.

es.L: Setenta sietes han sido decretados sobre tu pueblo y sobre tu santa ciudad, para terminar la transgresión, y para sellar el pecado, y para expiar la iniquidad, y para traer la justicia eterna, y para sellar la visión y el profeta, y para ungir un [lugar] santísimo.
es.B: Setenta sietes han sido decretados para tu pueblo y tu santa ciudad, para poner fin a la rebelión, para acabar con el pecado, para expiar la maldad, para traer una justicia eterna, para sellar la visión y la profecía, y para ungir un lugar santísimo.
es.R: Dios ha fijado un tiempo de setenta grupos de siete para tu pueblo y tu santa ciudad. En ese tiempo Dios pondrá fin a su rebeldía. Acabará con el pecado. Quitará la culpa. Traerá una justicia que durará para siempre. Hará que la visión y la profecía se cumplan. Y consagrará un lugar santísimo para Dios.

decisions.choice: seventy sevens: the number of periods, and the readings of 9:24-27
decisions.reason: The text gives the number and no unit: "sevens". The usual reading is seventy periods of seven years, 490 years, an extension of Jeremiah's seventy years (verse 2) by seven, perhaps after Leviticus 26:18, 21, 24, 28 ("seven times" for sins) and the sabbath years of Leviticus 25. How the 490 years are counted, and from when, is not stated. The "anointed one" of verses 25-26 has been read in several main ways: as Joshua the high priest of the return (Zechariah 3; 6:11), or Zerubbabel; as Cyrus, whom Isaiah 45:1 calls the LORD's anointed; as Onias III, the high priest killed in 171 BC, in the reading that places the last seven in the time of Antiochus IV; and, in Christian readings, as Jesus the Messiah, whose death is seen in "an anointed one will be cut off" (verse 26). The text settles none of these, and the translation does not choose among them.

decisions.choice: to finish the transgression, to seal up sin: to bring sin to an end
decisions.reason: "Finish" may mean to complete or to restrain. For "seal up", the Hebrew text as written reads "to seal up" (as later in the verse) and the text as read aloud reads "to bring to an end". Both say that the time of sin and its punishment will be closed.

decisions.choice: to seal up vision and prophet: to confirm the prophecy by fulfilling it
decisions.reason: To seal is to authenticate and to close. The vision and the prophet (that is, prophecy) will be confirmed when what they foretold comes to pass.

decisions.choice: to anoint a most holy place: the dedication of a holy place, or a holy person
alternatives: to anoint a most holy one
decisions.reason: "Holy of holies" (most holy) is used of the inner room of the tabernacle and temple, the altar and holy things (Exodus 26:33; 29:37; Ezekiel 45:3), never elsewhere of a person. So it is usually read as the consecration of the temple or its altar, in the usual reading the rededication of 164 BC or the restored temple of the end. Christian readers have also seen in it the anointing of Christ, the Holy One.

decisions.choice: seventy sevens (L, B); seventy sets of seven (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows the table for Daniel. "Sevens" keeps the Hebrew's lack of a unit (m1); Readable says "sets of seven" so that the number is not misread as seventy times seven. Literal brackets "place" in "a most holy [place]".

decisions.choice: God has set; God will ... He will (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who decreed the time and will do these things; the Hebrew uses a passive and infinitives. The pronoun "he" in these sentences is God's: plain "He" at the start of a sentence, and the deity_pronoun setting in the last sentence.

decisions.choice: "soixante-dix septaines" (L, B), "soixante-dix périodes de sept" (R), for 9:24-27; never "semaines"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets: the Hebrew gives a number of sevens and no unit, and "semaines" would choose a unit the text does not name. Readable, like the English "sets of seven", does not add "years" here.

decisions.choice: "un saint des saints" (L), "un lieu très saint" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no article; Literal keeps the indefinite phrase without capitals, since the meaning decision leaves open whether a place or a person is meant.

decisions.choice: "setenta sietes" (L, B); "setenta grupos de siete" (R)
decisions.reason: The text gives the number and no unit; Spanish never says "semanas" here, which would decide the reading. The same words through 9:25–27

decisions.choice: "rebeldía" (R)
decisions.reason: R keeps peshaʿ apart from the "pecado" that follows in the same list

source.text: וְתֵדַ֨ע וְתַשְׂכֵּ֜ל מִן־מֹצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר לְהָשִׁיב֙ וְלִבְנ֤וֹת יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עַד־מָשִׁ֣יחַ נָגִ֔יד שָׁבֻעִ֖ים שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְשָׁבֻעִ֞ים שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֗יִם תָּשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנְתָה֙ רְח֣וֹב וְחָר֔וּץ וּבְצ֖וֹק הָעִתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will know and you will understand: from [the] going out of [the] word to restore and to build Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince, sevens seven; and sevens sixty and two it will again be built, square and moat, and in distress of the times.

en.L: So know and understand: from the going out of the word to restore and to rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince, [there will be] seven sevens. And for sixty-two sevens it will be built again, with plaza and moat, but in times of distress.
en.B: Know and understand this: from the time the word goes out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed leader comes, there will be seven sevens. Then for sixty-two sevens it will be rebuilt, with streets and a trench, but in troubled times.
en.R: You must know and understand this. A command will be given to rebuild Jerusalem. From that time until a chosen leader comes, there will be seven sets of seven. Then for sixty-two sets of seven, Jerusalem will be rebuilt, with streets and a moat, but in times of trouble.

fr.L: Sache donc et comprends : depuis la sortie de la parole [ordonnant] de rétablir et de rebâtir Jérusalem jusqu’à un oint, un chef, [il y aura] sept septaines. Et pendant soixante-deux septaines elle sera rebâtie, place et fossé, mais dans la détresse des temps.
fr.B: Sache-le et comprends-le : depuis le moment où sortira l’ordre de rétablir et de rebâtir Jérusalem jusqu’à la venue d’un chef oint, il y aura sept septaines. Puis, pendant soixante-deux septaines, elle sera rebâtie, avec ses places et ses fossés, mais en des temps de détresse.
fr.R: Tu dois savoir et comprendre ceci. Un ordre sera donné de rebâtir Jérusalem. À partir de ce moment jusqu’à la venue d’un chef choisi par Dieu, il y aura sept périodes de sept. Puis, pendant soixante-deux périodes de sept, Jérusalem sera rebâtie, avec ses rues et son fossé, mais dans des temps difficiles.

es.L: Sabe, pues, y entiende: desde la salida de la palabra para restaurar y reedificar Jerusalén hasta un ungido, un príncipe, [habrá] siete sietes. Y durante sesenta y dos sietes volverá a ser edificada, con plaza y foso, pero en tiempos de angustia.
es.B: Debes saber y entender esto: desde que salga la palabra para restaurar y reconstruir Jerusalén hasta que venga un líder ungido, habrá siete sietes. Luego, durante sesenta y dos sietes, será reconstruida, con calles y foso, pero en tiempos difíciles.
es.R: Tienes que saber y entender esto. Se dará una orden para reconstruir Jerusalén. Desde ese momento hasta que venga un líder escogido, pasarán siete grupos de siete. Después, durante sesenta y dos grupos de siete, Jerusalén será reconstruida, con calles y un foso, pero en tiempos de dificultad.

decisions.choice: until an anointed one, a prince: seven sevens. Then sixty-two sevens
alternatives: until an anointed one, a prince, there will be seven sevens and sixty-two sevens; it will be built again ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew accents put the main pause of the verse after "seven sevens", so that the anointed prince comes after seven sevens, and the sixty-two sevens are the time in which the city is rebuilt. The translation follows that division. Read without the accents, the two numbers can be joined: "until an anointed one, a prince, [there will be] seven sevens and sixty-two sevens", sixty-nine sevens in all, which is how many Christian readers, following some ancient translations, have counted to the coming of Christ. See the note at verse 24.

decisions.choice: the going out of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem: the starting point of the count
decisions.reason: The "word" may be God's word (like the word of verse 23, or Jeremiah's prophecy of verse 2, given in 597 or 587 BC), or a king's decree: that of Cyrus (538 BC; Ezra 1:1-4), or later decrees under Artaxerxes (Ezra 7; Nehemiah 2, about 458 or 445 BC). The readings of verse 24 count from different starting points.

decisions.choice: an anointed one, a prince: an anointed leader
decisions.reason: Both words lack the article. "Anointed" is used of kings, priests and once of Cyrus (Isaiah 45:1); "prince" (nagid) means a leader or ruler, used of kings (1 Samuel 9:16) and of a chief priest (Nehemiah 11:11). On who is meant, see verse 24.

decisions.choice: plaza and moat: the open square and the defenses of the city
decisions.reason: The first word means the open square inside the gate; the second, a word found only here in the Bible, is usually taken as a trench or moat. Together they say the city will be fully rebuilt.

decisions.choice: an anointed one, a prince (L); an anointed leader (B); a chosen leader (R); no deity pronoun
decisions.reason: The wording follows the table for Daniel; Readable says "chosen" for anointed, as in Isaiah 45:1. The anointed one takes no deity_pronoun span, since the text does not settle who he is (verse 24).

decisions.choice: seven sevens, sixty-two sevens (L, B); sets of seven (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 24.

decisions.choice: "un oint, un chef" (L), "un chef oint" (B), "un chef choisi par Dieu" (R), lowercase and with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets: the text does not say who the anointed one is, and the meaning decision sets out the readings, so French chooses none of them.

decisions.choice: "un ungido, un príncipe" (L); "un líder ungido" (B); "un líder escogido" (R); no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the English levels; lowercase and without a span, so that the wording does not choose among the readings set out in the meaning decisions

source.text: וְאַחֲרֵ֤י הַשָּׁבֻעִים֙ שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֔יִם יִכָּרֵ֥ת מָשִׁ֖יחַ וְאֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ וְהָעִ֨יר וְהַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ יַ֠שְׁחִית עַ֣ם נָגִ֤יד הַבָּא֙ וְקִצּ֣וֹ בַשֶּׁ֔טֶף וְעַד֙ קֵ֣ץ מִלְחָמָ֔ה נֶחֱרֶ֖צֶת שֹׁמֵמֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And after the sevens sixty and two will be cut off an anointed one, and nothing [will be] to him; and the city and the sanctuary will destroy [the] people of a prince who is coming; and its end [will be] with the flood, and until [the] end war; [the] determined [things are] desolations.

en.L: And after the sixty-two sevens an anointed one will be cut off and will have nothing; and the city and the sanctuary the people of a prince who is to come will destroy. And its end [will come] with a flood, and to the end there will be war; desolations are decreed.
en.B: After the sixty-two sevens an anointed one will be cut off, left with nothing. The people of the ruler who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will come like a flood, and war will continue to the end; desolations have been decreed.
en.R: After the sixty-two sets of seven, someone who has been anointed will be killed and will have nothing. Then the army of a ruler who will come will destroy the city and the temple. The end will come like a flood. There will be war until the end. God has decided that there will be terrible destruction.

fr.L: Et après les soixante-deux septaines, un oint sera retranché, et il n’aura rien ; et la ville et le sanctuaire, le peuple d’un chef qui viendra les détruira. Et sa fin [viendra] avec l’inondation, et jusqu’à la fin, la guerre ; les ruines sont décrétées.
fr.B: Après les soixante-deux septaines, un oint sera retranché, et il ne lui restera rien. Le peuple d’un chef qui doit venir détruira la ville et le sanctuaire. Sa fin viendra comme une inondation, et la guerre durera jusqu’à la fin : des ruines ont été décrétées.
fr.R: Après les soixante-deux périodes de sept, quelqu’un qui a reçu l’onction sera tué, et il n’aura plus rien. Ensuite, l’armée d’un chef qui viendra détruira la ville et le temple. La fin viendra comme une inondation. Il y aura la guerre jusqu’à la fin. Dieu a décidé qu’il y aurait une terrible destruction.

es.L: Y después de los sesenta y dos sietes será cortado un ungido, y no tendrá nada; y a la ciudad y al santuario los destruirá el pueblo de un príncipe que ha de venir. Y su fin [será] con inundación, y hasta el fin habrá guerra; las desolaciones están decretadas.
es.B: Después de los sesenta y dos sietes, un ungido será quitado de en medio y se quedará sin nada. El pueblo del gobernante que ha de venir destruirá la ciudad y el santuario. Su fin llegará como una inundación, y la guerra continuará hasta el fin; las desolaciones ya han sido decretadas.
es.R: Después de los sesenta y dos grupos de siete, alguien que ha sido ungido será asesinado y no tendrá nada. Luego el ejército de un gobernante que vendrá destruirá la ciudad y el templo. El fin vendrá como una inundación. Habrá guerra hasta el fin. Dios ha decidido que habrá una destrucción terrible.

decisions.choice: an anointed one will be cut off: put to death or removed from office
decisions.reason: "Cut off" is used of being killed (Genesis 9:11; Jeremiah 11:19) and of being removed. On who the anointed one is, see verse 24: readers have taken him as Onias III, killed in 171 BC, or as Jesus the Messiah, among others.

decisions.choice: and will have nothing: a short and hard phrase
alternatives: and no one will be with him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "and there is not to him". It may mean that he will have nothing (no kingdom, no help), or that he will have no one, or, as some ancient translations take it, that it will be "not for himself". Some think a word is missing.

decisions.choice: the people of the prince who is to come: the forces of a coming ruler
decisions.reason: "Prince" (nagid) is the word used in verse 25, but this is a different ruler, who destroys the city. In the usual reading he is Antiochus IV, whose forces attacked Jerusalem and defiled the sanctuary; others see the Romans, who destroyed the temple in AD 70. The text names no one.

decisions.choice: its end with a flood: an overwhelming end
decisions.reason: A flood is a picture of an army sweeping over a land (Isaiah 8:7-8; 11:22). "Its end" may be the city's or the prince's.

decisions.choice: someone who has been anointed will be killed (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "killed" for "cut off", the sense that most readers take, and "someone who has been anointed" so as not to say whether this is the same anointed one as in verse 25. No deity_pronoun span is used (verse 25).

decisions.choice: the army of a ruler; God has decided (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "army" for the people of the ruler, and names God as the one who decreed the desolations.

decisions.choice: "será cortado" (L); "será quitado de en medio" (B); "será asesinado" (R)
decisions.reason: L keeps the Hebrew verb; B leaves open death or removal, as the meaning decision does; R follows the English R

source.text: וְהִגְבִּ֥יר בְּרִ֛ית לָרַבִּ֖ים שָׁב֣וּעַ אֶחָ֑ד וַחֲצִ֨י הַשָּׁב֜וּעַ יַשְׁבִּ֣ית׀זֶ֣בַח וּמִנְחָ֗ה וְעַ֨ל כְּנַ֤ף שִׁקּוּצִים֙ מְשֹׁמֵ֔ם וְעַד־כָּלָה֙ וְנֶ֣חֱרָצָ֔ה תִּתַּ֖ךְ עַל־שֹׁמֵֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he will make strong a covenant with the many [for] seven one; and [in the] middle of the seven he will make cease sacrifice and offering; and on a wing of abominations [will be] one desolating, and until complete destruction, and what is determined will be poured out on the desolated.

en.L: And he will make a strong covenant with the many for one seven; and in the middle of the seven he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on a wing of abominations [will come] one who makes desolate, until the complete destruction that is decreed is poured out on the one who makes desolate."
en.B: He will make a firm covenant with many for one seven. In the middle of the seven he will put a stop to sacrifice and offering. And on a wing of the temple will be the abomination that brings ruin, until the end that has been decreed is poured out on the one who brings ruin."
en.R: That ruler will make a strong agreement with many people for one set of seven years. But halfway through that time he will stop the sacrifices and offerings. He will set up the horrible thing that brings ruin on a high part of the temple. He will do this until the end that God has decided is poured out on him."

fr.L: Et il affermira une alliance avec la multitude [pendant] une septaine ; et au milieu de la septaine il fera cesser le sacrifice et l’offrande. Et sur une aile des abominations [viendra] celui qui dévaste, jusqu’à ce que la destruction complète qui est décrétée se déverse sur celui qui dévaste. »
fr.B: Il conclura une alliance solide avec beaucoup de gens pour une septaine. Au milieu de la septaine, il fera cesser le sacrifice et l’offrande. Et sur une aile du temple se dressera l’abomination qui apporte la ruine, jusqu’à ce que la fin décrétée se déverse sur celui qui apporte la ruine. »
fr.R: Ce chef fera une alliance solide avec beaucoup de gens pour une période de sept ans. Mais au milieu de cette période, il arrêtera les sacrifices et les offrandes. Il installera la chose horrible qui détruit sur une partie élevée du temple. Il fera cela jusqu’à ce que la fin que Dieu a décidée se déverse sur lui. »

es.L: Y confirmará un pacto con los muchos [por] un siete; y a la mitad del siete hará cesar el sacrificio y la ofrenda. Y sobre un ala de abominaciones [vendrá] uno que causa desolación, hasta que la destrucción completa, que está decretada, se derrame sobre el desolador».
es.B: Hará un pacto firme con muchos por un siete. A la mitad del siete pondrá fin al sacrificio y a la ofrenda. Y sobre un ala del templo estará la abominación que trae la ruina, hasta que el fin decretado se derrame sobre el que trae la ruina».
es.R: Ese gobernante hará un acuerdo firme con mucha gente por un período de siete años. Pero a la mitad de ese tiempo hará que cesen los sacrificios y las ofrendas. Pondrá la cosa horrible que trae la ruina en una parte alta del templo. Lo hará hasta que caiga sobre él el fin que Dios ha decidido».

decisions.choice: he will make a strong covenant: the coming prince of verse 26
decisions.reason: The nearest person before "he" is the prince who is to come (verse 26), and most read it so: a ruler who makes a firm agreement with many, then breaks it. In the usual reading this is Antiochus IV, supported by Jews who abandoned the covenant (11:30-32; 1 Maccabees 1:11-15). Some Christian readers take "he" to be the anointed one, who confirms a covenant; others, a final enemy at the end. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: he will put an end to sacrifice and offering
decisions.reason: The stopping of the temple sacrifices is the act of the small horn in 8:11 and of the king in 11:31 and 12:11. In the usual reading it is the suppression of the temple worship by Antiochus IV in 167 BC, about three and a half years before the temple was cleansed (compare "a time, times and half a time", 7:25).

decisions.choice: on a wing of abominations, one who makes desolate: the abomination that makes desolate
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one taken up in 11:31 and 12:11, "the abomination that makes desolate", here in a fuller and harder form. "Abominations" is the word used for idols and idolatrous things (1 Kings 11:5; 2 Kings 23:13). "Wing" may mean a high part or corner of the temple, or the wing of the altar, or the abominations may be pictured as borne on wings; some ancient translations read "on the temple". The usual reading sees the pagan altar set up on the altar of burnt offering in 167 BC (1 Maccabees 1:54, which uses the same phrase).

decisions.choice: the abomination that makes desolate: Matthew 24:15 and Mark 13:14
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of "the abomination of desolation, spoken of through Daniel the prophet" standing in the holy place, as a sign for those in Judea to flee (Matthew 24:15; Mark 13:14). He takes up Daniel's words for what was still to come. The Gospels quote the Greek form of the phrase.

decisions.choice: on the one who makes desolate: the destroyer is himself destroyed
decisions.reason: The last word is the same verb as before: the end that God has decreed falls on the desolator. Some read it as "on the desolate", meaning the ruined city, but the first fits the end of the small horn and the king (7:26; 8:25; 11:45).

decisions.choice: on a wing of abominations [will come] one who makes desolate (L); the abomination that brings ruin (B); the horrible thing that brings ruin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the table's wording for the phrase, the wording of Matthew 24:15 at those levels (and of Mark 13:14 at Balanced). Literal follows the fuller Hebrew of this verse, with its plural "abominations" and "one who makes desolate", which the table's Literal wording, "the abomination that makes desolate", gives where the Hebrew has the short form (11:31; 12:11).

decisions.choice: That ruler; seven years; a high part of the temple; God has decided (R)
decisions.reason: Readable takes the usual readings of m1 and m3 and says them plainly; they are uncertain, as the meaning decisions say. It says "seven years" for "one seven", the usual reading of the unit (verse 24).
